question: Can an already motivated positive projector action select Q_anchor from the 15 or 28 rank-four J-invariant sector projections?

normalization.projectorClass: rank-four diagonal projections formed from two complete rank-two J-orbits
normalization.dirac: unit coefficient on every primitive edge of the quotient support graph and its J partner
normalization.cutIdentity: S_cut is exactly the number of quotient edges crossing the selected two-vertex set
normalization.distanceAction: graph distance between the two selected quotient vertices
normalization.volumeAction: (1/2) Tr(Q D^2), equal to the sum of the selected quotient degrees for unit J-paired state edges
normalization.anchorPenalty: S_mu(Q)=S_cut(Q)+mu(1-(1/2)Tr(P_B Q)), mu>0, where P_B projects onto B=IN/NI

target.markedPhysicalMeaning: the already declared selected-cofactor P role under the claim-1548 descent dictionary

twelveStateModel.result: The unweighted Dirichlet/cut action already selects Q_anchor uniquely.

sixteenStateSectorRepair.unmarkedDegeneracyExplanation: AB, DG and FH are the three terminal two-vertex branches, each separated by one edge.
sixteenStateSectorRepair.result: The intrinsic unweighted cut action leaves a threefold degeneracy; marking only B lifts it and selects AB for every mu>0.

commutingPositiveFunctionals.representedAlgebra: Tr([Q,pi(a)]^*[Q,pi(a)])=0 for every candidate and every a in C^6
commutingPositiveFunctionals.reason: all candidates and these operators are diagonal in the occupied-sector basis

weightedBoundary.intrinsicConclusion: positive but unequal primitive coefficients can select any terminal branch; positivity alone does not canonically prefer AB
weightedBoundary.singleAnchorLimitation: a B-penalty cannot distinguish AB from another B-containing pair, so for arbitrary unequal weights it does not universally force AB
weightedBoundary.unitWeightConclusion: with the minimal isotropic normalization, every mu>0 makes AB the unique global minimizer on both models

minimalExtraDatum.datum: one already physically named rank-two J-orbit P_B, or equivalently the hard condition B is contained in Q
minimalExtraDatum.informationAdded: one marked orbit, not the desired two-orbit support
minimalExtraDatum.whyMinimal: all unmarked intrinsic diagonal symmetry tests vanish, and the repaired graph has three equal terminal branches under the unit cut action
minimalExtraDatum.cost: the mark uses the claim-1548 physical descent dictionary; without accepting that dictionary it is new correspondence data
minimalExtraDatum.forbiddenPrimitiveSupport: none; the functional evaluates existing edges and adds no Dirac matrix element

decision.H12IntrinsicSelection: SAT under the unit/isotropic primitive-edge normalization
decision.H16IntrinsicSelection: UNSAT because of the AB/DG/FH threefold minimum
decision.H16SingleMarkedOrbitSelection: SAT for every mu>0 under the same unit normalization
decision.strongestConclusion: The Dirichlet cut action is a genuine dynamical selector on H12. The minimal H16 repair creates two indistinguishable terminal competitors; one previously declared physical anchor orbit is sufficient to restore uniqueness without specifying A, but this is conditional correspondence data rather than a derivation of the full anchor from C^6 alone.

boundary: The exhaustive result covers all diagonal rank-four J-invariant two-orbit projections in the explicit 12-state and 16-state new-sector models. It does not classify non-diagonal rank-four projections in the full Grassmannian or derive equality of primitive edge norms from a spectral action.
